original_question: For parking problems on random trees, especially in regimes involving heavy-tailed car-arrival distributions and frozen modifications of the Erdos-Renyi process, can one prove scaling-limit results in Gromov-weak or Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov type metric topologies, and do the resulting limits relate to additive and multiplicative coalescents or to inhomogeneous continuum random trees?
target_in_paper: The nearest paper-faithful target is not a numbered conjecture but the informal open problem in Section 5, “Future directions: metric topologies, connections to random planar maps and open problems of Lackner and Panholzer,” especially the paragraph on page 14 asking for extensions of parking on random trees to heavy-tailed regimes and to frozen Erdős–Rényi-type settings, with scaling limits in Gromov-weak or Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov-type topologies and possible links to additive/multiplicative coalescents and inhomogeneous continuum random trees. The heavy-tail hypothesis needed to make this precise is supplied by the conjectural regime summarized in Section 4 after Proposition 5 on page 12.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s main future-direction theme: parking on random trees in heavy-tailed regimes, interaction with frozen modifications of Erdős–Rényi, the search for scaling limits in metric-measure topologies, and the expected relation to coalescent limits and inhomogeneous continuum random trees. It also correctly treats this as an open problem rather than an established theorem.
missing_details: The paper does not state a numbered conjecture here; the closest match is an informal future-direction paragraph in Section 5, so the question should not present this as an official theorem-level conjecture.

The heavy-tail assumption in the paper is more specific than “heavy-tailed car-arrival distributions”: either the offspring distribution of the tree or the car-arrival distribution should have infinite third moment and tail asymptotic c·k^{-γ} for some c > 0 and γ in (3,4) as k→∞ (Section 4, p. 12).
The paper explicitly says the conjectured critical behavior concerns both strongly connected and weakly connected components; your draft omits this distinction (Section 4, p. 12).

The critical size scale conjectured in the paper is that component sizes should be of order n^{(γ−2)/(γ−1)} at criticality; without this scale the scaling-limit question is underspecified (Section 4, p. 12).

The paper distinguishes two nearby frozen models: the frozen configuration model in Contat (2023) and the frozen modification of Erdős–Rényi in Contat–Curien (2023). Your draft merges them; a faithful reformulation should either separate them or explicitly say one is asking for a combination suggested by Section 5.
The topology should be specified as acting on suitably rescaled parked components/clusters viewed as rooted measured metric spaces; otherwise “scaling-limit results” is too vague.

The paper’s proven topology-level precedent is Theorem 4, which gives Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov hypograph convergence for fully parked trees under standing assumptions such as boundedness, exchangeability, branching, and aperiodicity; your draft does not say that the proposed heavy-tail question lies beyond that proven bounded setting (Section 4, p. 13).

The candidate limits are presented only as expected analogies in the survey: a combination of additive and multiplicative coalescent behavior and possible relation to inhomogeneous continuum random trees. The paper does not assert an already-formulated exact limiting object here.
If the question is meant to stay close to the paper, it should mention criticality explicitly; Section 5 discusses these topology questions in the context of critical scaling phenomena.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or “for all sufficiently large m” clause is relevant here; the missing structure is probabilistic (tree model, component type, tail exponent, critical scaling, topology, and candidate limit object), not algebraic.
refined_question: At criticality, for parking on random trees in a regime where either the offspring distribution or the car-arrival distribution has infinite third moment and tail c·k^{-γ} with c > 0 and γ in (3,4), and especially when this heavy-tailed regime is combined with the frozen modification of the Erdős–Rényi process, can one prove that the strong or weak parked components—conjecturally of size order n^{(γ−2)/(γ−1)}—admit nontrivial scaling limits as rooted measured metric spaces in Gromov-weak or Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov-type topologies, and can one identify the limiting objects in terms of additive/multiplicative coalescent behavior or inhomogeneous continuum random trees?
justification: The draft is closest to the Section 5 future-directions paragraph on page 14, which explicitly mentions heavy-tail extensions, frozen Erdős–Rényi, Gromov-weak and Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov topologies, additive and multiplicative coalescents, and inhomogeneous continuum random trees. To make that open problem stand alone and paper-faithful, one must import the only precise heavy-tail hypothesis given nearby: the conjectural regime summarized after Proposition 5 on page 12, namely infinite third moment with tail c·k^{-γ}, γ in (3,4), for either the offspring or arrival distribution, together with the conjectured critical component scale n^{(γ−2)/(γ−1)}. Theorem 4 on page 13 gives the paper’s nearest proven topology-level analogue, but only in a bounded/exchangeable fully parked setting, so the refined question is framed as an extension beyond that theorem rather than as a restatement of it.
